# MASTER SUPPLY AGREEMENT

This Master Supply Agreement (this "**Agreement**" or this "**Master Supply Agreement**") is entered into as of March 1, 2026 (the "**Effective Date**") by and between **Tessaline Polymers LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company ("**Supplier**"), and **Harrowgate Provisions, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation ("**Customer**"). Supplier and Customer are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

A. Supplier manufactures and sells food-grade flexible packaging film and related converted products.

B. Customer produces packaged food products and wishes to buy packaging film from Supplier for use in its operations.

C. The Parties wish to set out the terms on which Supplier will supply, and Customer will purchase, such products. These terms are supplemented by one or more Order Forms and by the Quality Agreement.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants in this Agreement, the Parties agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

1.1 **Definitions.** The following terms have the following meanings in this Agreement:

(a) "**Affiliate**" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a Party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the entity or the power to direct its management and policies.

(b) "**Artwork**" means all graphics, text, logos, trademarks, nutritional and ingredient statements, allergen declarations, regulatory statements and other printed matter that Customer provides or approves for printing on Products.

(c) "**Change of Control**" means, for any Party: (i) the acquisition by any person or group, directly or indirectly, of beneficial ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting equity of that Party; (ii) any merger, consolidation, share exchange or similar transaction involving that Party, whether or not that Party is the surviving entity, after which the holders of that Party's voting equity immediately before the transaction hold less than fifty percent (50%) of the voting equity of the surviving or resulting entity or its ultimate parent; or (iii) the sale of all or substantially all of the assets of that Party.

(d) "**Customer Materials**" means Artwork, Customer's trademarks, and any specifications, designs or other materials Customer provides to Supplier for use in making Products.

(e) "**Filled Product**" means any food or other product that Customer or its designee packages in, fills into or seals with Products.

(f) "**Losses**" means all losses, damages, liabilities, judgments, settlements, fines, penalties, costs and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees, arising from a Third-Party Claim.

(g) "**Order Form**" means Order Form No. 1 dated as of the Effective Date between the Parties, and any later order form signed by both Parties that references this Agreement. Each Order Form sets out, among other things, the term, pricing and volume commitments for the Products covered by it.

(h) "**Products**" means the packaging film products described in the applicable Order Form and the Specifications.

(i) "**Purchase Order**" means a written or electronic order for Products issued by Customer under this Agreement and an Order Form.

(j) "**Quality Agreement**" means the Quality Agreement between the Parties dated as of the Effective Date, which sets out the Specifications and the inspection, acceptance, rejection and warranty-claim procedures for Products, as amended from time to time.

(k) "**Specifications**" means the technical, material, performance and food-contact specifications for each Product set out in or incorporated into the Quality Agreement.

(l) "**Third-Party Claim**" means any claim, suit, action or proceeding brought by a person other than a Party or its Affiliates.

1.2 **Interpretation.** Headings are for convenience only. "Including" means "including without limitation." References to Sections are to Sections of this Agreement unless otherwise stated. References to "days" mean calendar days unless "business days" is specified.

1.3 **Order of Precedence.** The Order Form and the Quality Agreement are incorporated into this Agreement by reference. If the terms of these documents conflict, they shall govern in the following order of precedence: Order Form, then Master Supply Agreement, then Quality Agreement. The pre-printed terms of any Purchase Order, acknowledgment, invoice or similar document shall have no effect, even if accepted or signed.

## 2. TERM

2.1 **Term.** This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for the Initial Term, and any Renewal Term, stated in the Order Form, unless terminated earlier under Section 14.

2.2 **Survival of Orders.** If this Agreement expires or is terminated, any Purchase Order accepted before the effective date of expiration or termination shall remain governed by this Agreement until fulfilled, unless the Purchase Order is cancelled under Section 14.

## 3. FORECASTS AND ORDERS

3.1 **Forecasts.** On or before the fifth (5th) business day of each calendar month, Customer shall give Supplier a non-binding rolling forecast of its expected Product requirements for the following six (6) months.

3.2 **Purchase Orders.** Customer shall order Products by issuing Purchase Orders that state the Product, quantity, requested delivery date and delivery location. Supplier shall accept or reject each Purchase Order in writing within three (3) business days after receipt. Supplier may not unreasonably reject a Purchase Order that matches the most recent forecast and the lead times in the Order Form. A Purchase Order not rejected within that period is deemed accepted.

3.3 **Changes.** Customer may change the quantity or delivery date of an accepted Purchase Order by written notice at least ten (10) business days before the scheduled ship date. Supplier shall use commercially reasonable efforts to accommo

## 4. PRICING AND PAYMENT

4.1 **Prices.** Customer shall pay for Products at the prices set out in the applicable Order Form. Prices are stated in U.S. dollars and include standard packaging for shipment. Prices may be adjusted only as provided in the Order Form.

4.2 **Invoicing and Payment.** Supplier shall invoice Customer upon shipment of each order. Customer shall pay each invoice within 45 days after receipt of undisputed invoice. Payment shall be made by ACH or wire transfer to the account Supplier designates in writing.

4.3 **Disputed Amounts.** Customer may withhold payment of any amount it disputes in good faith if it notifies Supplier in writing of the disputed amount and the reasons before the payment due date. Customer shall timely pay any undisputed portion. The Parties shall work in good faith to resolve the dispute within thirty (30) days.

4.4 **Late Payment.** Undisputed amounts not paid when due bear interest at the lesser of one percent (1%) per month and the highest rate permitted by law, from the due date until paid.

4.5 **Taxes.** Prices exclude sales, use, excise, value-added and similar taxes, which Customer shall pay unless it provides a valid exemption certificate. Each Party is responsible for taxes on its own income, property and employees.

## 5. DELIVERY, TITLE AND RISK OF LOSS

5.1 **Delivery.** Unless the Order Form states otherwise, Supplier shall deliver Products FCA Supplier's facility (Incoterms 2020) to the carrier Customer designates, on the delivery date stated in the accepted Purchase Order.

5.2 **Late Delivery.** Supplier shall notify Customer promptly if it expects any delay in delivery. If Supplier fails to deliver within five (5) business days after the scheduled date for reasons other than Customer's acts or a Force Majeure Event, Customer may (a) cancel the affected portion of the Purchase Order without liability, or (b) require Supplier to ship by expedited means at Supplier's cost.

5.3 **Title and Risk.** Title and risk of loss pass to Customer upon delivery to the carrier in accordance with Section 5.1.

5.4 **Packaging and Labeling for Shipment.** Supplier shall package, mark and palletize Products in accordance with the Specifications and good industry practice for food-contact materials, so as to prevent contamination and damage in transit.

## 6. QUALITY

6.1 **Quality Agreement.** Supplier shall manufacture, test, store and ship Products in accordance with the Quality Agreement. Inspection, acceptance, rejection of nonconforming lots, and warranty-claim procedures are governed by the Quality Agreement.

6.2 **Regulatory Compliance.** Supplier shall ensure that Products, and the materials used to make them, comply with all laws applicable to food-contact packaging in the United States, including 21 C.F.R. Parts 174 through 186 and applicable FDA food-contact notifications.

6.3 **Change Control.** Supplier shall not change any raw material, resin or additive supplier, manufacturing site or material process for a Product without at least ninety (90) days' prior written notice to Customer and Customer's written approval, as further provided in the Quality Agreement.

6.4 **Audits.** On reasonable prior notice and during normal business hours, Customer or its designee may audit Supplier's facilities, records and quality systems relating to Products, no more than once per calendar year except for cause.

## 7. WARRANTIES

7.1 **Product Warranty.** Supplier warrants that each Product, upon delivery and for the warranty period stated in the Quality Agreement, will (a) conform to the Specifications, (b) be free from defects in materials and workmanship, (c) be manufactured in compliance with applicable law and current good manufacturing practices, and (d) be suitable for direct food contact as described in the Specifications.

7.2 **Title.** Supplier warrants that it will convey good title to the Products, free of all liens and encumbrances.

7.3 **Customer Warranties.** Customer warrants that (a) it has the right to provide the Customer Materials to Supplier for use under this Agreement, and (b) the Artwork, as provided or approved by Customer, will comply with applicable labeling laws.

7.4 **Remedies.** Customer's remedies for breach of Section 7.1 are set out in the Quality Agreement, together with any remedies available under Section 10.1.

7.5 **Disclaimer.** EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS AGREEMENT OR THE QUALITY AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY OTHER WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

## 8. CUSTOMER MATERIALS AND ARTWORK

8.1 **Supply of Artwork.** Customer shall provide Artwork in the format specified by Supplier and shall review and approve each proof in writing before Supplier begins production.

8.2 **Accuracy.** Supplier shall reproduce approved Artwork faithfully within the print tolerances stated in the Specifications. Supplier is not responsible for the content of approved Artwork, including any errors in ingredient, allergen or nutritional statements.

8.3 **Tooling.** Printing plates, cylinders and other tooling made specifically for Customer's Artwork and paid for by Customer are Customer's property. Supplier shall hold them in good condition and return them to Customer on request.

## 9. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

9.1 **Ownership.** Each Party retains all right, title and interest in its own intellectual property. Customer owns all rights in the Customer Materials. Supplier owns all rights in its film formulations, processes and know-how.

9.2 **License to Supplier.** Customer grants Supplier a non-exclusive, non-transferable, royalty-free license during the Term to use the Customer Materials solely to manufacture and supply Products to Customer.

9.3 **No Other Use.** Supplier shall not sell or supply to any third party any product bearing Customer's Artwork or trademarks.

## 10. INDEMNIFICATION

10.1

**By Supplier.** Supplier shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates and their officers, directors, employees and agents from and against all Losses arising out of any Third-Party Claim to the extent arising from (a) any defect in a Product or failure of a Product to conform to the Specifications or applicable law, (b) any claim that a Product, excluding Customer Materials, infringes or misappropriates any patent, copyright, trademark or trade secret of a third party, or (c) the negligence or willful misconduct of Supplier or its personnel.

10.2 **By Customer.** Customer shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Supplier, its Affiliates and their officers, directors, employees and agents from and against all Losses arising out of any Third-Party Claim to the extent arising from (a) any claim that the Artwork or other Customer Materials infringe or misappropriate any patent, copyright, trademark or trade secret of a third party, (b) the content of any labeling or Artwork, including ingredient, allergen, nutritional and regulatory statements, (c) the contents of any Filled Product, including any product liability, personal injury, illness or recall claim relating to a Filled Product, except to the extent caused by a Product's failure to conform to the Specifications, or (d) the negligence or willful misconduct of Customer or its personnel.

10.3 **Procedure.** The Party seeking indemnification shall (a) give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of the Third-Party Claim, though a delay in notice relieves the indemnifying Party of its obligations only to the extent it is materially prejudiced, (b) give the indemnifying Party sole control of the defense and settlement, but the indemnifying Party may not settle any claim that admits fault or imposes non-monetary obligations on the indemnified Party without its written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, and (c) provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense. The indemnified Party may participate with counsel of its own choosing at its own expense.

10.4 **Infringement Remedies.** If a Product becomes, or in Supplier's reasonable opinion is likely to become, the subject of an infringement claim covered by Section 10.1(b), Supplier may at its option and expense (a) procure the right for Customer to continue using the Product, or (b) modify or replace the Product so that it is non-infringing while still conforming to the Specifications.

## 11. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

11.1 **Exclusion of Consequential Damages.** EXCEPT AS PROVIDED IN SECTION 11.3 AND SECTION 11.4, NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, OR FOR LOST PROFITS OR LOST REVENUE, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, HOWEVER CAUSED AND UNDER ANY THEORY OF LIABILITY, EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES.

11.2 **Cap on Liability.** EXCEPT AS PROVIDED IN SECTION 11.3 AND SECTION 11.4, EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, WHETHER IN CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, SHALL NOT EXCEED THE fees paid or payable in the prior 12 months BY CUSTOMER TO SUPPLIER UNDER THIS AGREEMENT, MEASURED FROM THE DATE OF THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM.

11.3 **Exceptions.** Sections 11.1 and 11.2 do not apply to (a) a Party's liability for fraud, gross negligence or willful misconduct, (b) a Party's breach of Section 13 (Confidentiality), or (c) Customer's obligation to pay amounts due for Products under Section 4.

11.4 **Customer Indemnity.** Notwithstanding Section 11.2 or Section 11.1, Customer's obligations under Section 10.2 shall not be subject to any limitation of liability or exclusion of damages set out in this Agreement.

## 12. INSURANCE

12.1 **Coverage.** During the Term and for two (2) years afterward, each Party shall maintain, with insurers rated A- VII or better by A.M. Best: (a) commercial general liability insurance, including products and completed operations coverage, with limits of at least $5,000,000 per occurrence and in the aggregate; (b) product recall insurance with limits of at least $2,000,000; and (c) workers' compensation insurance as required by law.

12.2 **Certificates.** Each Party shall provide certificates of insurance to the other on request and shall give at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice of any cancellation or material reduction in coverage.

## 13. CONFIDENTIALITY

13.1 **Obligations.** Each Party shall keep confidential all non-public information disclosed by the other Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential, including pricing, Specifications, formulations and forecasts ("**Confidential Information**"). The receiving Party shall use Confidential Information only to perform this Agreement and shall disclose it only to its and its Affiliates' employees, advisors and financing sources who need to know it and are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as this Section 13.

13.2 **Exclusions.** Confidential Information excludes information that (a) is or becomes public through no fault of the receiving Party, (b) was known to the receiving Party without restriction before disclosure, (c) is independently developed without use of the disclosing Party's Confidential Information, or (d) is rightfully received from a third party without restriction.

13.3 **Compelled Disclosure.** The receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information as required by law or court order, if it gives the disclosing Party prompt notice, where lawful, and reasonable cooperation in seeking a protective order.

13.4 **Duration.** The obligations in this Section 13 continue during the Term and for five (5) years afterward, and for trade secrets for as long as they remain trade secrets under applicable law.

## 14. TERMINATION

14.1 **Termination for Breach.** Either Party may terminate this Agre

ement by written notice if the other Party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure the breach within thirty (30) days after receiving written notice describing it.

14.2 **Insolvency.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement immediately by written notice if the other Party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, has a receiver appointed for its business, or becomes the subject of any bankruptcy proceeding that is not dismissed within sixty (60) days.

14.3 **Effect of Termination.** Upon expiration or termination: (a) Customer shall pay for all Products delivered before the effective date and for any finished Products and Customer-specific raw materials held by Supplier for Customer within the forecast and lead-time limits in the Order Form; (b) Supplier shall return all tooling and Customer Materials; and (c) each Party shall return or destroy the other Party's Confidential Information.

14.4 **Survival.** Sections 4, 7, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14.3, 14.4, 15 and 17, and any other provision that by its nature should survive, survive expiration or termination.

## 15. ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL

15.1 **Assignment by Supplier.** Supplier may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without the consent of Customer, to any person, and may delegate any of its obligations under this Agreement to any Affiliate or subcontractor. Supplier shall notify Customer in writing within thirty (30) days after any such assignment.

15.2 **Assignment by Customer.** Customer may not assign, delegate or otherwise transfer this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations under it, whether voluntarily, by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of Supplier.

15.3 **Change of Control of Customer.** Any Change of Control of Customer, including by merger in which Customer is the surviving entity, shall be deemed an assignment of this Agreement by Customer requiring the prior written consent of Supplier under Section 15.2. If a Change of Control of Customer occurs without the prior written consent of Supplier, Supplier may, at any time within one hundred eighty (180) days after it learns of the Change of Control, terminate this Agreement on thirty (30) days' written notice to Customer. In that event, the unpaid balance of the minimum annual purchase commitment under the Order Form for the remainder of the then-current term shall become immediately due and payable by Customer.

15.4 **Void Transfers; Binding Effect.** Any purported assignment or transfer in violation of this Section 15 is void. Subject to this Section 15, this Agreement binds and benefits the Parties and their respective successors and permitted assigns.

## 16. NOTICES

16.1 **Method.** All notices under this Agreement must be in writing and are effective when delivered by hand, one (1) business day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier, or upon confirmed transmission by email if a copy is also sent by one of the other methods, to the addresses below or another address a Party designates by notice:

**If to Supplier:**
Tessaline Polymers LLC
4410 Brandywine Commerce Drive
Wilmington, Delaware 19803
Attention: General Counsel
Email: legal@tessalinepolymers.com

**If to Customer:**
Harrowgate Provisions, Inc.
900 Mill Race Parkway
Lancaster, Pennsylvania 17601
Attention: Chief Legal Officer
Email: legalnotices@harrowgateprovisions.com

## 17. GENERAL

17.1 **Governing Law.** This Agreement, and any claim arising out of or relating to it, is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply.

17.2 **Jurisdiction.** Each Party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New Castle County, Delaware, for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and waives any objection to venue in those courts.

17.3 **Force Majeure.** Neither Party is liable for any failure or delay in performance, other than payment obligations, caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including acts of God, fire, flood, war, terrorism, epidemic, governmental action or widespread utility failure (each, a "**Force Majeure Event**"), provided it promptly notifies the other Party and uses commercially reasonable efforts to resume performance. If a Force Majeure Event affecting Supplier continues for more than sixty (60) days, Customer may cancel affected Purchase Orders and source the affected Products elsewhere without liability.

17.4 **Independent Contractors.** The Parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency or employment relationship.

17.5 **Amendment and Waiver.** This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by both Parties. No waiver is effective unless in writing and signed by the waiving Party, and no failure or delay in exercising any right operates as a waiver of it.

17.6 **Severability.** If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain in full force, and the invalid provision shall be enforced to the maximum extent permitted by law.

17.7 **Counterparts.** This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together are one instrument.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Master Supply Agreement as of the Effective Date.

# ORDER FORM NO. 1

**Under the Master Supply Agreement dated as of March 1, 2026**

This Order Form No. 1 (this "**Order Form**") is entered into as of March 1, 2026 (the "**Effective Date**") by and between **Tessaline Polymers LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company ("**Supplier**"), and **Harrowgate Provisions, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation ("**Customer**"). It is issued under, and forms part of, the Master Supply Agreement between the Parties dated as of the Effective Date (the "**Master Supply Agreement**").

## 1. INCORPORATION AND DEFINITIONS

1.1 **Incorporation.** This Order Form is an "Order Form" as defined in Section 1.1(g) of the Master Supply Agreement. It is incorporated into the Master Supply Agreement by reference in accordance with Section 1.3 of the Master Supply Agreement.

1.2 **Definitions.** Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Order Form have the meanings given to them in the Master Supply Agreement. In this Order Form:

(a) "**Contract Year**" means each consecutive twelve (12) month period during the Term. The first Contract Year begins on the Effective Date.

(b) "**Initial Term**" has the meaning given in Section 2.1.

(c) "**Renewal Term**" has the meaning given in Section 2.2.

(d) "**Resin Index**" means the monthly average contract price for low-density polyethylene film-grade resin, as published by the resin price reporting service the Parties designate in writing, or a substantially equivalent successor index the Parties agree on in writing.

(e) "**Term**" means the Initial Term together with any Renewal Terms.

## 2. TERM AND RENEWAL

2.1 **Initial Term.** The initial term of the Master Supply Agreement and this Order Form begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years from the Effective Date (the "**Initial Term**"), unless terminated earlier under Section 14 or Section 15.3 of the Master Supply Agreement.

2.2 **Renewal.** At the end of the Initial Term, the Master Supply Agreement and this Order Form shall automatically renew for successive five (5) year Renewal Terms (each, a "**Renewal Term**"). They shall continue to renew at the end of each Renewal Term unless either Party gives the other Party written notice of non-renewal. A notice of non-renewal is effective only if it is delivered in accordance with Section 16 of the Master Supply Agreement no earlier than sixty (60) days and no later than thirty (30) days before the end of the Initial Term or the then-current Renewal Term. A notice delivered outside that period is of no effect, and the Master Supply Agreement and this Order Form shall renew as provided in this Section 2.2. Except as the Parties otherwise agree in writing, all terms of this Order Form, including the minimum annual purchase commitment in Section 3.1 and the pricing mechanism in Section 4, shall apply during each Renewal Term.

## 3. VOLUME COMMITMENTS

3.1 **Minimum Annual Purchase Commitment.** During each Contract Year, Customer shall purchase Products from Supplier with an aggregate invoiced value, net of taxes, freight and credits for rejected Products, of at least $2,400,000 (the "**Minimum Annual Purchase Commitment**").

3.2 **Credit Toward Commitment.** The following count toward the Minimum Annual Purchase Commitment for the Contract Year in which they would have shipped: (a) Products ordered under an accepted Purchase Order that Supplier fails to deliver for any reason other than Customer's breach; (b) Products cancelled by Customer under Section 5.2 or Section 17.3 of the Master Supply Agreement; and (c) Products rejected as nonconforming under the Quality Agreement and not replaced by Supplier within the time required by the Quality Agreement.

3.3 **Shortfall.** Within sixty (60) days after the end of each Contract Year, Supplier shall deliver to Customer a statement showing the invoiced value of Products purchased during that Contract Year, as adjusted under Section 3.2. If the adjusted amount is less than the Minimum Annual Purchase Commitment, Supplier may invoice Customer for twenty percent (20%) of the difference (the "**Shortfall Payment**"). The Shortfall Payment is payable in accordance with Section 4.2 of the Master Supply Agreement. The Parties agree that the Shortfall Payment is a reasonable estimate of Supplier's lost margin and is not a penalty.

3.4 **Capacity Reservation.** Supplier shall reserve production capacity sufficient to supply Customer's forecast requirements up to one hundred twenty-five percent (125%) of the Minimum Annual Purchase Commitment in each Contract Year, prorated by month. Supplier shall use commercially reasonable efforts to supply requirements above that level.

## 4. PRODUCTS AND PRICING

4.1 **Products and Prices.** The Products covered by this Order Form and their initial prices are set out below. All Products shall conform to the Specifications in the Quality Agreement.

| Part No. | Product Description | Gauge | Unit | Price per Unit (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP-LF-2140 | Clear LDPE/LLDPE coextruded lidding film, heat-seal coated | 2.0 mil | 1,000 sq. ft. | $38.50 |
| TP-BF-3325 | High-barrier EVOH multilayer forming film, thermoform grade | 3.25 mil | 1,000 sq. ft. | $71.20 |
| TP-PR-1875 | Reverse-printed PET/PE laminate rollstock, up to 8 colors | 1.875 mil | 1,000 sq. ft. | $54.75 |
| TP-SW-1200 | Anti-fog polyolefin shrink overwrap film | 1.2 mil | 1,000 sq. ft. | $22.90 |

4.2 **Plate and Cylinder Charges.** Supplier shall charge Customer for new printing plates and cylinders for TP-PR-1875 at Supplier's documented cost plus ten percent (10%), quoted in writing and approved by Customer before ordering. Tooling paid for by Customer is Customer's property under Section 8.3 of the Master Supply Agreement.

4.3 **Price Adjustment.** Prices are fixed for the first Contract Year. After that, either Party may request a price adjustment once per calendar quarter, by written notice with supporting data, if the Resin Index average for the

order_form_no1.md, page 2 of 2:
preceding calendar quarter has moved by more than five percent (5%) up or down from the Resin Index average for the quarter on which current prices were based. The adjustment shall equal the percentage change in the Resin Index multiplied by the resin share of the Product price, which the Parties agree is fifty-five percent (55%) for each Product. Adjusted prices apply to Purchase Orders issued thirty (30) days or more after the notice. No other price increase is permitted without Customer's written agreement.

4.4 **Most Favored Pricing.** If, during the Term, Supplier sells a substantially similar product to another customer in comparable volumes and on comparable terms at a lower unit price, Supplier shall promptly offer that lower price to Customer for the corresponding Product.

## 5. ORDERING, LEAD TIMES AND DELIVERY

5.1 **Lead Times.** Supplier's standard lead times from acceptance of a Purchase Order to shipment are: (a) fifteen (15) business days for TP-LF-2140 and TP-SW-1200; (b) twenty (20) business days for TP-BF-3325; and (c) twenty (20) business days for TP-PR-1875 using existing approved Artwork, or thirty (30) business days for new Artwork after proof approval.

5.2 **Minimum Order Quantities.** The minimum quantity per Purchase Order line is 250 units (1,000 sq. ft. each) per Part No., or 400 units for any new print run of TP-PR-1875.

5.3 **Forecast Liability.** Customer is responsible under Section 14.3(a) of the Master Supply Agreement only for (a) finished Products made to fill accepted Purchase Orders, and (b) Customer-specific raw materials, including printed inventory and custom-formulated resin, purchased by Supplier to meet the first two (2) months of Customer's most recent forecast, up to a maximum value equal to two (2) months of average monthly purchases over the preceding six (6) months.

5.4 **Delivery.** Products shall be delivered FCA Supplier's facility at 4410 Brandywine Commerce Drive, Wilmington, Delaware 19803 (Incoterms 2020), or another Supplier facility approved by Customer under Section 6.3 of the Master Supply Agreement, to the carrier Customer designates.

5.5 **Safety Stock.** Supplier shall maintain at its cost a safety stock of finished TP-LF-2140 and TP-BF-3325 equal to at least two (2) weeks of Customer's average forecast requirements for each. Supplier shall rotate safety stock on a first-in, first-out basis so that no Product is shipped more than six (6) months after its date of manufacture.

## 6. ACCOUNT MANAGEMENT

6.1 **Contacts.** Each Party shall designate an account manager responsible for the day-to-day relationship under this Order Form. The account managers shall meet, in person or by videoconference, at least once each calendar quarter to review forecasts, delivery performance, quality metrics and pricing.

6.2 **Performance Reporting.** Supplier shall provide Customer a monthly report showing on-time-in-full delivery performance, open Purchase Orders, safety stock levels and any quality events reported under the Quality Agreement.

## 7. GENERAL

7.1 **Effect.** Except as expressly provided in this Order Form, the Master Supply Agreement remains in full force and effect and governs the purchase and sale of the Products listed in Section 4.1.

7.2 **Amendment.** This Order Form may be amended only by a written instrument signed by both Parties, in accordance with Section 17.5 of the Master Supply Agreement.

7.3 **Counterparts.** This Order Form may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together are one instrument.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Order Form No. 1 as of the Effective Date.

**TESSALINE POLYMERS LLC**

By: ______________________________
Name: Damian R. Okafor
Title: Chief Executive Officer

**HARROWGATE PROVISIONS, INC.**

By: ______________________________
Name: Lillian M. Pryce
Title: President and Chief Executive Officer

# QUALITY AGREEMENT

This Quality Agreement (this "**Quality Agreement**") is entered into as of March 1, 2026 (the "**Effective Date**") by and between **Tessaline Polymers LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company ("**Supplier**"), and **Harrowgate Provisions, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation ("**Customer**"). It is the "Quality Agreement" referred to in the Master Supply Agreement between the Parties dated as of the Effective Date (the "**Master Supply Agreement**").

## 1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE

1.1 **Purpose.** This Quality Agreement sets out the Specifications and the quality responsibilities of the Parties for the Products. It covers manufacturing controls, inspection, acceptance, rejection of nonconforming lots, warranty-claim procedures, change control, complaints and recalls.

1.2 **Scope.** This Quality Agreement applies to all Products supplied under the Master Supply Agreement and any Order Form. As of the Effective Date, the Products are Part Nos. TP-LF-2140, TP-BF-3325, TP-PR-1875 and TP-SW-1200, as listed in Section 4.1 of Order Form No. 1.

1.3 **Relationship to Master Supply Agreement.** This Quality Agreement is incorporated into the Master Supply Agreement by reference under Section 1.3 of the Master Supply Agreement. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Quality Agreement have the meanings given to them in the Master Supply Agreement.

## 2. DEFINITIONS

In this Quality Agreement:

(a) "**Certificate of Analysis**" or "**CoA**" means a document issued by Supplier for each Lot that states the test results for the Lot against each release parameter in the applicable Product Specification Sheet.

(b) "**Deviation**" means any departure from the Specifications, approved processes or this Quality Agreement during manufacture, testing, storage or shipment of a Product.

(c) "**Latent Defect**" means a nonconformity that could not reasonably be detected by the incoming inspection described in Section 6.1.

(d) "**Lot**" means a quantity of a single Part No. made in one continuous production run from the same raw material lots and identified by a unique lot number.

(e) "**Nonconforming Product**" means any Product that does not conform to the Specifications or to the warranties in Section 7.1 of the Master Supply Agreement.

(f) "**Product Specification Sheet**" means the specification sheet for a Part No. described in Section 3.1, as approved in writing by both Parties.

## 3. SPECIFICATIONS

3.1 **Product Specification Sheets.** The Specifications for each Product consist of the Product Specification Sheet for that Part No., attached as Schedule A, together with the general requirements in Section 3.2. Each Product Specification Sheet states at least the following: resin and layer structure; nominal gauge and gauge tolerance; width and roll dimensions; core size; tensile strength; elongation; seal strength and seal initiation temperature; oxygen and moisture vapor transmission rates, where applicable; coefficient of friction; haze and gloss; and, for TP-PR-1875, color standards and print registration tolerances.

3.2 **General Requirements.** All Products shall:

(a) be manufactured only from resins, additives, inks, adhesives and coatings that comply with 21 C.F.R. Parts 174 through 186 or are the subject of an effective FDA food-contact notification for the intended conditions of use;

(b) be free of foreign matter, gels and carbon specks above the limits in the Product Specification Sheet, pinholes, delamination and odor or taint transfer;

(c) for TP-PR-1875, meet a residual solvent limit of not more than 10 mg/m² total retained solvents; and

(d) be wound, wrapped and palletized as required by Section 5.4 of the Master Supply Agreement and the Product Specification Sheet.

3.3 **Changes to Specifications.** A Product Specification Sheet may be changed only by a written revision signed by the quality representatives of both Parties named in Section 10. Each revision shall bear a new revision number and effective date.

## 4. MANUFACTURING AND QUALITY SYSTEM

4.1 **Quality Management System.** Supplier shall maintain a quality management system certified to a Global Food Safety Initiative-benchmarked standard for packaging manufacturers, such as BRCGS Packaging Materials or FSSC 22000, and shall keep that certification current throughout the Term. Supplier shall notify Customer within five (5) business days if its certification is suspended, withdrawn or downgraded.

4.2 **Good Manufacturing Practices.** Supplier shall manufacture, test, store and ship Products in accordance with current good manufacturing practices for food-contact packaging, including documented hygiene, pest control, glass and brittle plastics, foreign-matter and allergen-segregation programs.

4.3 **Release Testing.** Supplier shall test each Lot against the release parameters in the applicable Product Specification Sheet before shipment. Supplier shall not ship any Lot that fails a release parameter, unless Customer has approved a written deviation under Section 4.5.

4.4 **Certificates of Analysis.** Supplier shall provide a CoA for each Lot by email no later than the time of shipment. Each roll and pallet shall be labeled with the Part No., Lot number, date of manufacture and roll number.

4.5 **Deviations.** Supplier shall record and investigate every Deviation. Supplier shall not ship any Product affected by a Deviation that may affect conformity to the Specifications unless Customer's quality representative has approved the Deviation in writing before shipment. Customer's approval of a Deviation applies only to the Lots identified in the approval.

## 5. WARRANTY MECHANICS

5.1 **Warranty Period.** The warranty period for the purposes of Section 7.1 of the Master Supply Agreement is 18 months after delivery of the applicable Lot. The warranty period applies to Products stored by Customer in accordance with the storage conditions stated in the Product Specification Sheet.

5.2 **Warranty

Claims.** Customer may make a warranty claim for any Nonconforming Product, including a Latent Defect, discovered at any time during the warranty period. Customer shall submit each claim in writing to Supplier's quality representative within fifteen (15) business days after discovering the nonconformity. The claim shall identify the Part No., Lot number and nature of the nonconformity and, where practicable, include photographs or samples.

5.3 **Investigation.** Supplier shall acknowledge each warranty claim within two (2) business days and shall deliver a written root-cause analysis and corrective and preventive action plan within twenty (20) business days after receipt of the claim. Customer shall make retained samples available to Supplier on request.

5.4 **Remedies.** For any Nonconforming Product, Supplier shall, at Customer's election: (a) replace the Nonconforming Product at Supplier's cost within ten (10) business days after Customer's election; or (b) issue a credit or refund of the price paid for the Nonconforming Product. In either case Supplier shall bear the cost of return freight and disposal of the Nonconforming Product. These remedies are in addition to any remedies available under Section 10.1 of the Master Supply Agreement, as provided in Section 7.4 of the Master Supply Agreement.

## 6. INSPECTION, ACCEPTANCE AND REJECTION

6.1 **Incoming Inspection.** Customer may inspect each Lot upon receipt. Incoming inspection may include review of the CoA, visual inspection of rolls and packaging, and sample testing of the parameters in the Product Specification Sheet.

6.2 **Rejection Window.** Customer may reject any Lot that is nonconforming by written notice to Supplier within 10 business days after delivery. The notice shall state the reasons for rejection. A Lot not rejected within that period is deemed accepted for purposes of incoming inspection only. Acceptance does not affect Customer's rights under Section 5 for Latent Defects or for any nonconformity discovered during the warranty period.

6.3 **Disputed Rejections.** If Supplier disputes a rejection, the Parties' quality representatives shall confer within five (5) business days. If they cannot agree, the Parties shall jointly submit retained samples to an independent laboratory accredited to ISO/IEC 17025 that is acceptable to both Parties. The laboratory's results are binding on the Parties as to conformity. The Party whose position is not supported by the results shall pay the laboratory's fees.

6.4 **Handling of Rejected Lots.** Customer shall quarantine rejected Lots and hold them for Supplier's inspection for up to twenty (20) business days after the rejection notice. Supplier shall then arrange for collection or authorize disposal at its cost. Supplier shall replace rejected Lots in accordance with Section 5.4.

## 7. CHANGE CONTROL

7.1 **Notified Changes.** In accordance with Section 6.3 of the Master Supply Agreement, Supplier shall give Customer at least ninety (90) days' prior written notice of, and obtain Customer's written approval for, any change to: (a) any raw material, resin, additive, ink, adhesive or coating, or the supplier of any of them; (b) the manufacturing site or production line; or (c) any material process step or test method.

7.2 **Qualification.** Each change notice shall include a description of the change, the reason for it, an updated food-contact compliance statement and proposed validation data. On request, Supplier shall supply qualification samples from at least three (3) production Lots made under the changed conditions. Customer shall respond to a complete change notice within sixty (60) days and shall not unreasonably withhold approval.

## 8. COMPLAINTS, NOTIFICATIONS AND RECALLS

8.1 **Notification of Quality Events.** Each Party shall notify the other within twenty-four (24) hours after becoming aware of any information suggesting that a Product shipped to Customer may present a food-safety risk, including contamination, migration above regulatory limits or a material Deviation.

8.2 **Recalls.** Customer has sole authority to decide whether to conduct a recall, market withdrawal or stock recovery of any Filled Product. Supplier shall cooperate fully with Customer in any recall, including by providing Lot traceability data, retained samples and test results within twenty-four (24) hours after Customer's request. Responsibility for the costs of a recall is determined under the Master Supply Agreement.

8.3 **Traceability.** Supplier shall maintain traceability from each Lot to the raw material lots used in it, and shall be able to complete a full trace within four (4) hours. Supplier shall conduct a mock recall at least once each calendar year and share the results with Customer.

## 9. AUDITS AND RECORDS

9.1 **Audits.** Customer's audit rights are set out in Section 6.4 of the Master Supply Agreement. For any audit, Supplier shall make available its quality manual, batch records, CoAs, Deviation and complaint records, calibration records and third-party audit reports. Supplier shall respond in writing to audit findings within thirty (30) days with a corrective action plan.

9.2 **Records Retention.** Supplier shall retain all batch records, CoAs, test data and Deviation records for each Lot for at least three (3) years after the end of the warranty period for that Lot.

9.3 **Retained Samples.** Supplier shall retain a representative sample of each Lot, stored under the conditions in the Product Specification Sheet, until the end of the warranty period for that Lot.
